Messages.Author: Morgan Vening
Messages.Body:
These questions seem covered by the rules, but before I utilise them,
I wanted to seek 'clarification'.

Torn Signpost
The way it is written in it's latest incarnations, it seems to give
you a strength boost, but doesn't in any way count as a strike. So
making Strength based Hand damage strikes, or even some weapon
strikes, seem to benefit. Is that how it's interpreted? (and if so,
does that mean, for example, that the Vampire superglues his Meat
Cleaver to his torn signpost before he whacks with it, or does it mean
the Vampire has so much civil pride, that seeing a torn signpost turns
him into a raving psychopath?)

'Blocking' Window
The apparent assertion at our group is that there is a blocking window
(opportunity to block), that can be missed. An example, as has
happened on many an occasion.
P1 - I bleed with Vampire X. Do you block?
P2 - Nope.
P1 - In that case, Conditioning.
P2 - Ouch. *removes 4+ pool*

But the way the rules imply, this isn't the case. Once an Action
Modifier or Reaction is played, everyone who is able, can then respond
with further cards. In other words, an action is only completed when
both players pass consecutively?

Morgan Vening

Messages.Body:

> These questions seem covered by the rules, but before I utilise them,

> Torn Signpost
> The way it is written in it's latest incarnations, it seems to give
> you a strength boost, but doesn't in any way count as a strike. So
> making Strength based Hand damage strikes, or even some weapon
> strikes, seem to benefit. Is that how it's interpreted? (and if so,
> does that mean, for example, that the Vampire superglues his Meat
> Cleaver to his torn signpost before he whacks with it, or does it mean
> the Vampire has so much civil pride, that seeing a torn signpost turns
> him into a raving psychopath?)

At superior potence, Torn signpost gives you Strength 3.
Meat cleaver strikes for strength+1.
Total damage from strike: 3+1 = 4.

> 'Blocking' Window
> The apparent assertion at our group is that there is a blocking window
> (opportunity to block), that can be missed. An example, as has
> happened on many an occasion.
> P1 - I bleed with Vampire X. Do you block?
> P2 - Nope.
> P1 - In that case, Conditioning.
> P2 - Ouch. *removes 4+ pool*

That is correct. P2 can still play deflection, telepathic counter, etc.
Anything (including wakes with evenings freshness but not
Rat's warning) that does not require blocking.

> But the way the rules imply, this isn't the case. Once an Action
> Modifier or Reaction is played, everyone who is able, can then respond
> with further cards. In other words, an action is only completed when
> both players pass consecutively?

Once a player has declared that they are not blocking,
they cannot revise that decision unless the bleed is directed
back to them. The decision to block does not prevent
the playing of further cards, but those cards do not alter the
choice not to block.

-JTP

Messages.Author: Izaak
Messages.Body:
> Torn Signpost
> The way it is written in it's latest incarnations, it seems to give
> you a strength boost, but doesn't in any way count as a strike. So
> making Strength based Hand damage strikes, or even some weapon
> strikes, seem to benefit. Is that how it's interpreted? (and if so,
> does that mean, for example, that the Vampire superglues his Meat
> Cleaver to his torn signpost before he whacks with it, or does it mean
> the

The Torn Signpost represents the vampires fury. He's so angry/strong (or
both), that he has torn a signpost apart on his way to the opposing
minion.
So yes, it stacks with melee weapons and the like. It's a temporary
strength bonus.

>Vampire has so much civil pride, that seeing a torn signpost turns
> him into a raving psychopath?)

No, he's such a raving psychopath that he has torn a signpost apart as
warm-up.

> 'Blocking' Window
> The apparent assertion at our group is that there is a blocking window
> (opportunity to block), that can be missed. An example, as has
> happened on many an occasion.
> P1 - I bleed with Vampire X. Do you block?
> P2 - Nope.
> P1 - In that case, Conditioning.
> P2 - Ouch. *removes 4+ pool*

The above is correct. You can attempt to block or decline to block. If
you decline, you can no longer attempt to block the action, even if it's
modefied by, for example, a conditioning.

> But the way the rules imply, this isn't the case. Once an Action
> Modifier or Reaction is played, everyone who is able, can then respond
> with further cards. In other words, an action is only completed when
> both players pass consecutively?

No. Blocking attempts are not affected by modifiers or reaction cards.
That's the whole point of action modfiers. You either block, or you
don't. You get one shot at deciding that.

All this gets kinda icky when cards like Eagle's Sight kick in. Once a
Methusalah declines to block, he's no longer eligable to block, unless
the target of the action changes (by, for example, a card like
Deflection). And now that there's a thread about blocking anyway, let me
just ask this to the knowlegdable crowd:

Often, this is seen:

Meth 1: I bleed with vampire X. Block?
Meth 2: Nope.
Meth 1: Conditioning
Meth 3: Wait up, Eagle's Sight and I block
Meth 1: Hey, we were already past blocking...
*argument starts and a judge is needed*

Or this:

Meth 1: I bleed with vampire X. Block?
Meth 2: Nope.
Meth 1: Anyone ELSE wants to block?
Other Meths: you can't ask that to us. We're by default not eligable to
block this action, so of course we're not blocking
Meth 1: very well, Conditioning
Meth 3: Hold up, Eagle's Sight and block attempt
*huge argument starts about who already declined to block etc etc*

I'd say that both can be argued for as correct play, but the former is
fair play from the acting Meth, while the latter is kind of a loophole
that shouldn't be there. Preventing Eagle blocks by asking if anyone
else wants to block is, IMO, not fair and also not entirely correct. You
can't ask a player if he wants to play a Deflection either, so that he
"already declined" before you play the modifier.

My take on it is this:
The only ones having to decide whether to block or not are the ones that
CAN block the action in the first place. No need to ask your predator if
he wants to block a bleed, or ask you grandprey if he wants to block an
equip action. If they want to, they can play their Eagle's Sight
whenever they want to, making them a legit blocker and only THEN the
whole block/decline to block thing starts.

Am I correct?

> Meth 2: Nope.
> Meth 1: Conditioning
> Meth 3: Wait up, Eagle's Sight and I block
> Meth 1: Hey, we were already past blocking...
> *argument starts and a judge is needed*

Meth 3 never declined to block, so can do so.

> Meth 1: I bleed with vampire X. Block?
> Meth 2: Nope.
> Meth 1: Anyone ELSE wants to block?
> Other Meths: you can't ask that to us. We're by default not eligable to
> block this action, so of course we're not blocking
> Meth 1: very well, Conditioning
> Meth 3: Hold up, Eagle's Sight and block attempt
> *huge argument starts about who already declined to block etc etc*

You can certainly ask if there are any other blocks. And if the Other
Meths say no, then Meth3 can't Eagle Sight because the block has already
been declined.

> Preventing Eagle blocks by asking if anyone
> else wants to block is, IMO, not fair and also not entirely correct.

How so? If the acting Meth asks, "Any other blocks?" and you say "no",
you've declined. Eagle sight allows you to block things you normally
couldn't; it doesn't let you, eg, block only if the acting Meth plays
Conditioning.

> You
> can't ask a player if he wants to play a Deflection either, so that he
> "already declined" before you play the modifier.

Playing a reaction card != blocking.

> My take on it is this:
> The only ones having to decide whether to block or not are the ones that
> CAN block the action in the first place. No need to ask your predator if
> he wants to block a bleed, or ask you grandprey if he wants to block an
> equip action. If they want to, they can play their Eagle's Sight
> whenever they want to, making them a legit blocker and only THEN the
> whole block/decline to block thing starts.
>
> Am I correct?

You are sadly mistaken.

--Colin McGuigan
